subject: math
title: Numbers to 50: Count, Tens and Ones, Compare
seo_title: Grade 1 Numbers to 50 Math Worksheets: Ten Frames, Tens and Ones, Free with Answer Key (Ontario)
standard_text: Read and represent whole numbers up to and including 50, and describe various ways they are used in everyday life
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 math worksheets on numbers to 50 for the Ontario curriculum: count objects and ten frames, tens and ones with base ten blocks, number words to twenty, compare and order numbers, and number lines and word problems. 100 questions with pictures and an answer key.
key_big: Count the tens first, then the ones. 3 tens and 4 ones is 34.
key_sub: Write the tens digit first: 1 ten and 3 ones is 13, not 31. To compare, look at the tens first: 31 is greater than 29.
body_html:
Count each thing once

Touch each thing as you count it. Count each thing only once. Groups of 5 and 10 make counting fast.

Ten frames

A ten frame has 10 boxes. A full ten frame is 1 ten. The empty boxes tell you how many more make 10.

Tens and ones

A rod is 10. A small cube is 1. Count the rods by tens. Then count on the cubes.

Write the tens first, then the ones. 34 = 30 + 4.

Tens and ones

What number is 2 tens and 8 ones?

2 tens is 20. 8 more ones make 28.

Answer: 28

Read and write number words

NumberWordNumberWord
11eleven16sixteen
12twelve17seventeen
13thirteen18eighteen
14fourteen19nineteen
15fifteen20twenty

In “fourteen” you hear the 4 first. But you write the 1 ten first: 14.

Compare and order

Look at the tens first. More tens means a greater number. If the tens are the same, look at the ones.

Which is greater?

Which is greater, 23 or 32?

23 has 2 tens. 32 has 3 tens.

Answer: 32

Number lines

On a number line, numbers get bigger to the right. Find a number you know. Then count the marks.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing 31 for 13Write the tens first: 1 ten and 3 ones is 13
Counting one thing twiceTouch each thing once, or cross it off
Reading tens as ones (3 rods and 4 cubes = 7)Each rod is 10: 10, 20, 30, then 31 to 34
Writing 1 ten and 3 ones as 103Use only 2 digits: 13
Saying 210 after 29After 29 comes a new ten: 30
Thinking a longer row has moreCount both rows. Spread-out things can be fewer

faq.q: What numbers should a Grade 1 student know in Ontario?
faq.a: In the Ontario curriculum, Grade 1 students read, write and show whole numbers up to 50. They also break numbers into tens and ones and compare and order numbers to 50.

faq.q: How do ten frames help Grade 1 students?
faq.a: A ten frame shows 10 in two rows of 5, so children see amounts at a glance and see how many more make 10. Two full frames and 4 more is 24.

faq.q: Why does my child write 31 for 13?
faq.a: In words like “thirteen” you hear the 3 first, so children write it first. Build 13 with 1 rod and 3 cubes, then say “1 ten first, then 3 ones” while writing 13.

faq.q: What are base ten blocks in Grade 1 math?
faq.a: Base ten blocks are the place value tools used in Ontario classrooms. A rod is 10 and a small cube is 1, so 3 rods and 4 cubes show 34.

items.q: How many apples?
items.e: The first 5 make a group. Count on: 6. Touch each one only once. There are 6 apples. 7 or 8 means an apple was counted twice.

items.q: How many counters are in the ten frame?
items.e: Count the counters, not the empty boxes. The top row has 5. Count on: 6, 7. There are 7 counters. 3 is the number of empty boxes.
The first 5 make a group. Count on: 6, 7, 8, 9. Touch each one only once. There are 9 stars. 4 counts only the stars after the group of 5.

items.q: How many more counters make 10?
items.e: Count the empty boxes: there are 4. 6 and 4 make 10. 6 is how many counters there are now.

items.q: How many counters are in the ten frame?
items.e: Count the counters, not the empty boxes. The top row has 5. Count on: 6, 7, 8, 9. There are 9 counters. 1 is the number of empty boxes.

items.q: How many more counters make 10?
items.e: Count the empty boxes: there are 7. 3 and 7 make 10.
Each full row has 10. Count the rows by tens: 10. Then count on: 11. There are 11 buttons. Do not write 2. The first row is 1 ten, not 1.

items.q: How many balls?
items.e: Each full row has 10. Count the rows by tens: 10. Then count on: 11, 12. There are 12 balls. Write the tens first: 12, not 21.

items.q: How many counters are there?
items.e: Each full ten frame is 10. Count by tens: 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13, 14. There are 14 counters. A full frame is 1 ten, not 1 counter.

items.q: How many apples?
items.e: Each full row has 10. Count the rows by tens: 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. There are 15 apples. Write the tens first: 15, not 51.

items.q: How many counters are there?
items.e: Each full ten frame is 10. Count by tens: 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17. There are 17 counters. A full frame is 1 ten, not 1 counter.

items.q: How many pucks?
items.e: Each full row has 10. Count the rows by tens: 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18. There are 18 pucks. Write the tens first: 18, not 81.

items.q: How many more counters make 20?
items.e: The first frame is full. The second frame has 3 counters and 7 empty boxes. 13 and 7 make 20.

items.q: How many counters are there?
items.e: Both ten frames are full. Count by tens: 10, 20. There are 20 counters. 2 tens is 20, not 2.

items.q: How many more counters make 20?
items.e: The second frame has 5 counters and 5 empty boxes. 15 and 5 make 20.

items.q: How many balls?
items.e: Each full row has 10. Count the rows by tens: 10, 20. Then count on: 21, 22, 23. There are 23 balls. Write the tens first: 23, not 32.
Each full ten frame is 10. Count by tens: 10, 20. Then count on: 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26. There are 26 counters. A full frame is 1 ten, not 1 counter.
Each full row has 10. Count the rows by tens: 10, 20. Then count on: 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27. There are 27 stars. Write the tens first: 27, not 72.
All 3 ten frames are full. Count by tens: 10, 20, 30. There are 30 counters.
Each full ten frame is 10. Count by tens: 10, 20, 30. Then count on: 31, 32. There are 32 counters. A full frame is 1 ten, not 1 counter.

sets.title: Tens and ones with rods and cubes

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: Each rod is 10. Count the rods by tens: 10. Then count on the cubes: 11, 12, 13. 1 ten and 3 ones is 13. Write the tens first, then the ones: 13, not 31 or 103.

items.q: How many tens are there?
items.e: Each rod is 1 ten. There are 2 rods. So there are 2 tens. The number is 26.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: Each rod is 10. Count the rods by tens: 10, 20. Then count on the cubes: 21, 22, 23, 24, 25. 2 tens and 5 ones is 25. Write the tens first, then the ones: 25, not 52 or 205.

items.q: How many ones are there?
items.e: Each small cube is 1 one. There are 4 cubes. So there are 4 ones. The number is 34.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: Each rod is 10. Count the rods by tens: 10, 20, 30. Then count on the cubes: 31. 3 tens and 1 one is 31. Write the tens first, then the ones: 31, not 13 or 301.

items.q: Which matches the blocks?
items.e: Count the rods: 2 tens. Count the cubes: 8 ones. That is 2 tens and 8 ones: 28.

items.q: 3 tens and 6 ones. What number is it?
items.e: 3 tens is 30. 6 more ones make 36. 3 + 6 = 9 adds the digits, not the tens and ones.
2 frames are full: 2 tens. The last frame has 7 counters: 7 ones. That is 2 tens and 7 ones. 3 is the number of empty boxes.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: Each rod is 10. Count by tens: 10, 20, 30, 40. There are no cubes, so write 0 ones: 40.

items.q: What number is 4 tens and 2 ones?
items.e: Write the tens digit first: 4. Then the ones digit: 2. The number is 42.

items.q: Which number has 1 ten and 9 ones?
items.e: Write the tens digit first: 1. Then the ones: 9. The number is 19. 91 has 9 tens.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: Each rod is 10. Count the rods by tens: 10, 20, 30, 40. Then count on the cubes: 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47. 4 tens and 7 ones is 47. Write the tens first, then the ones: 47, not 74 or 407.

items.q: 35 = 30 + ☐
items.e: 35 is 3 tens and 5 ones. The tens make 30. The ones make 5. So 35 = 30 + 5.

items.q: 28 = ☐ + 8
items.e: 28 is 2 tens and 8 ones. 2 tens is 20, not 2. So 28 = 20 + 8.

items.q: How many tens are in 40?
items.e: There are 4 bundles of 10 sticks: 10, 20, 30, 40. So 40 has 4 tens and 0 ones.

items.q: 5 bundles of 10 sticks. How many sticks?
items.e: Count by tens: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. 5 tens and 0 ones is 50.

items.q: Add 1 more rod. What number is it now?
items.e: The blocks show 23. A rod is 10, not 1. 23 and 10 more is 33. Only the tens digit changes.

items.q: Add 1 more cube. What number is it now?
items.e: The blocks show 19. 1 more cube makes 10 cubes. 10 cubes make 1 more ten. Now there are 2 tens and 0 ones: 20. Do not write 110.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: 1 rod is 10. There are 14 cubes. 10 cubes make 1 more ten, so 14 cubes are 1 ten and 4 ones. That is 2 tens and 4 ones: 24.

items.q: Which is another way to make 32?
items.e: Break 1 rod into 10 cubes. 3 tens and 2 ones become 2 tens and 12 ones. 20 and 12 make 32. The answer is 2 tens and 12 ones.

items.q: Which number is this?
items.e: Seven is the number after six. Write 7. Seventy is 70 and seventeen is 17.

items.q: How do you say this number?
items.e: 11 is 1 ten and 1 one. We say eleven.

items.q: Which number is this?
items.e: Twelve is 1 ten and 2 ones. Write 12. Twenty is 20.

items.q: What number is in the chart?
items.e: The chart shows 3 tens and 4 ones. Write the tens first, then the ones: 34.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Count on by 1: 23, 24, 25, 26. Only the ones digit changes.

items.q: Which number is this?
items.e: Fifteen is 1 ten and 5 ones. Write 15. Fifty is 50.

items.q: How do you say this number?
items.e: 13 is 1 ten and 3 ones. We say thirteen. Thirty is 30.

items.q: Count back. What number comes next?
items.e: The numbers go down by 1: 35, 34, 33, 32.

items.q: What number is in the chart?
items.e: The chart shows 4 tens and 1 one. Write the tens first, then the ones: 41.

items.q: Which number is this?
items.e: Fourteen is 1 ten and 4 ones. Write 14. You hear “four” first, but the 1 ten is written first.

items.q: How do you say this number?
items.e: 20 is 2 tens and 0 ones. We say twenty. Twelve is 12.

items.q: Maya’s class is in Room 17. Which digit is in the ones place?
items.e: 17 is 1 ten and 7 ones. The ones digit is the last digit: 7.

items.q: What number is missing?
items.e: Count on: 18, 19, 20, 21. After 19 comes a new ten: 20.

items.q: How do you say this number?
items.e: 18 is 1 ten and 8 ones. We say eighteen. Eighty is 80.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: After 29 comes 30. 9 ones and 1 more make a new ten. Do not write 210 or go back to 20.

items.q: Owen wears this hockey jersey. How many tens are in his number?
items.e: The number is 31. The 3 is in the tens place. 31 has 3 tens and 1 one.

items.q: What number comes just before 40?
items.e: Count back by 1 from 40: 40, 39. 30 is 10 less, not 1 less.

items.q: Which number has 2 tens?
items.e: The tens digit is the first digit. In 25 the 2 comes first, so it means 2 tens. The answer is 25. In 52, 12 and 32, the 2 means 2 ones.

items.q: Which list counts on by 1 the right way?
items.e: After 39 comes 40: 3 tens become 4 tens. The right list is 38, 39, 40.

items.q: What is 1 more than 49?
items.e: 1 more than 49 is 50. 9 ones and 1 more make a ten, so 4 tens become 5 tens.

items.q: Which row has more apples?
items.e: Count each row. Row A has 7. Row B has 9. 9 is more than 7, so Row B has more. Row A is longer, but its apples are far apart.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: All the numbers have 1 ten. Look at the ones: 9 is the most. 19 is the greatest.

items.q: Which row has fewer balls?
items.e: Count each row. Row A has 4. Row B has 6. 4 is less than 6, so Row A has fewer. Do not look at how long the row is.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: 20 has 2 tens, so it is not the least. 17, 12 and 15 have 1 ten. Look at the ones: 2 is the fewest. 12 is the least.
Row A has 8. Row B has 8. They are the same. Row B only looks longer.

items.q: Which blocks show the greater number?
items.e: A is 2 tens and 9 ones: 29. B is 3 tens and 1 one: 31. 3 tens is more than 2 tens, so B is greater. A has more pieces, but B has more tens.

items.q: Put the numbers in order from least to greatest.
items.e: 18 has 1 ten, 25 has 2 tens, 32 has 3 tens. The order is 18, 25, 32.

items.q: Which number is less than 20?
items.e: 18 has 1 ten. 20, 21 and 28 have 2 tens. So 18 is less than 20.

items.q: Which blocks show the smaller number?
items.e: A is 24. B is 42. 2 tens is less than 4 tens, so A is smaller.

items.q: Which number is greater than 30?
items.e: 34 has 3 tens and 4 ones. 30 has 3 tens and 0 ones. So 34 is greater than 30. 30 is equal to 30, not greater.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: On a number line, numbers get bigger to the right. 19 is to the left of 21. So 19 is less than 21.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Look at the tens first. 41 has 4 tens. The others have 1 or 3 tens. 41 is the greatest. 39 has more ones, but fewer tens.

items.q: Which blocks show the greater number?
items.e: Both have 3 tens. Look at the ones: A has 8 and B has 5. 38 is more than 35, so A is greater.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: Look at the tens first. 13 has only 1 ten. 13 is the least.

items.q: Put the numbers in order from greatest to least.
items.e: 40 and 41 have 4 tens. 41 has 1 more one, so it comes first. 14 has only 1 ten. The order is 41, 40, 14.

items.q: A shows 23. B shows 32. Which is true?
items.e: 23 has 2 tens. 32 has 3 tens. So 23 is less than 32.

items.q: Which number is between 25 and 30?
items.e: Between 25 and 30 come 26, 27, 28 and 29. 27 is one of them.

items.q: Put the numbers in order from least to greatest.
items.e: 27 has 2 tens, so it is the least. 30 and 36 have 3 tens. 0 ones is less than 6 ones. The order is 27, 30, 36.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: 50 has 5 tens. 45 and 49 have 4 tens. 5 has no tens. 50 is the greatest. 49 has 9 ones, but 50 has more tens.

items.q: Put the numbers in order from least to greatest.
items.e: 2 has no tens. 12 has 1 ten. 20 and 21 have 2 tens, and 20 has fewer ones. The order is 2, 12, 20, 21.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: Each small mark is 1. The long marks show the numbers ending in 5 and 0. Count from 5: 6, 7, 8. The arrow points to 8.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: Each small mark is 1. The long marks show the numbers ending in 5 and 0. Count from 10: 11, 12, 13. The arrow points to 13.

items.q: Which letter shows 27?
items.e: Find 25. Count on 2 marks: 26, 27. The letter is B. A is 23, which is 2 marks before 25.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: Each small mark is 1. The long marks show the numbers ending in 5 and 0. Count from 20: 21, 22. 12 is how far it is from 10. The arrow points to 22.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: Each small mark is 1. The long marks show the numbers ending in 5 and 0. It is 1 before 30. The arrow points to 29.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: Each small mark is 1. The long marks show the numbers ending in 5 and 0. Count from 35: 36. The arrow points to 36.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: Each small mark is 1. The long marks show the numbers ending in 5 and 0. Count from 45: 46, 47. The arrow points to 47.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: The numbers go up by 10. Each mark is 5, not 1. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35.

items.q: Emma sees 13 Canada geese. Then 1 more lands. How many now?
items.e: 1 more than 13 is 14. Count on 1: 13, 14.

items.q: Liam puts hockey pucks in rows of 10. How many pucks?
items.e: 2 full rows: 10, 20. Then count on: 21, 22, 23, 24. There are 24 pucks.

items.q: Leah has 18 beads. She needs 20. How many more?
items.e: There are 2 empty boxes. 18 and 2 make 20.

items.q: Nathan has 3 bundles of 10 sticks and 5 more. How many sticks?
items.e: Count the bundles by tens: 10, 20, 30. Count on: 31, 32, 33, 34, 35. He has 35 sticks.

items.q: Yesterday was day 29 of school. What day is today?
items.e: Today is 1 day after 29. After 29 comes 30.

items.q: Owen has 34 stickers. Ava has 43 stickers. Who has more?
items.e: 34 has 3 tens. 43 has 4 tens. 43 is more, so Ava has more.

items.q: Zoe’s class has 38 cans. Kai’s class has 32 cans. Which class has more?
items.e: Both have 3 tens. Look at the ones: 8 is more than 2. Zoe’s class has more.

items.q: Maya counts 40 leaves. Arjun counts 4 tens of leaves. Who has more?
items.e: 4 tens is 40. Maya has 40 and Arjun has 40. They are the same.

items.q: Chloe lives at number 14. Jayden lives at number 41. Whose number is greater?
items.e: 41 has 4 tens. 14 has 1 ten. 41 is greater, so Jayden’s number is greater. Both use a 1 and a 4, but the order matters.

items.q: Sofia’s number is between 30 and 40. It has 5 ones. What is it?
items.e: Between 30 and 40 means 3 tens. 3 tens and 5 ones is 35.

items.q: Benjamin has 27 hockey cards. Hana has 10 more. How many does Hana have?
items.e: 10 more adds 1 ten. 2 tens and 7 ones become 3 tens and 7 ones: 37. 28 is only 1 more.

items.q: Four friends count pine cones. Who has the most?
items.e: Look at the tens first. 41 has 4 tens. No one else has 4 tens. Mei has the most.
